text:
Marathon Petroleum ticked up 0.38% today to $435.12, capping a remarkably strong two-week rally of 11.66%. The stock's surge reflects a fundamental shift in refinery economics: crude oil prices have diverged sharply (US oil at $96/barrel versus global Brent at roughly $114), while diesel inventories remain tight and refineries are running at 92.5% capacity. Goldman Sachs signaled yesterday that diesel prices will stay elevated through 2027 due to capacity constraints, which translates directly into fatter profit margins for refiners like Marathon that can produce and sell diesel at premium prices.

The broader backdrop reinforces the tailwind. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Iranian tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz and the strategic contest over Red Sea shipping—are keeping global oil prices elevated and supply uncertainty on edge. Tight refinery capacity and high margins needed to rebuild diesel inventories mean refiners are positioned to capture outsized profits in the near term, even as the crude-to-product price spread widens.
